editorial_contributions.text:
Let \(O(n)\) be the orthogonal group of degree \(n\), and \(Q(n)\) the subgroup consisting of diagonal matrices with entries \(\pm 1\). Then the normalizer \(B_{n} := N_{O(n)} (Q(n))\) of \(Q(n)\) in \(O(n)\) is isomorphic to the wreath product \(O(1) \wr S_{n}\), where \(S_{n}\) is the symmetric group on \(n\) letters. In other words, it is the hyperoctahedral group, or the Coxeter group of type \(B_{n}\). Then the \textit{real unordered complete flag manifold} is defined as the homogeneous space \(\overline{\mathrm{Fl}}_{n}(\mathbb{R}) := O(n)/B_{n}\). Let \(\mathrm{Fl}_{n}(\mathbb{R}) = O(n)/Q(n)\) be the usual real complete flag manifold. An element of \(\mathrm{Fl}_{n}(\mathbb{R})\) can be identified with the ordered \(n\)-tuple of mutually orthogonal lines through the origin in \(\mathbb{R}^{n}\). Then the symmetric group \(S_{n}\) acts naturally on \(\mathrm{Fl}_{n}(\mathbb{R})\) by permuting these \(n\) lines, and \(\overline{\mathrm{Fl}}_{n}(\mathbb{R})\) can be identified with \(\mathrm{Fl}_{n}(\mathbb{R})\) by this action: \(\overline{\mathrm{Fl}}_{n}(\mathbb{R}) \cong \mathrm{Fl}_{n}(\mathbb{R})/S_{n}\). Similarly, one can define the complete flag manifold \(\mathrm{Fl}_{n}(\mathbb{C}) = U(n)/T(n)\), where \(U(n)\) is the unitary group of degree \(n\) and \(T(n)\) its maximal torus. The \textit{complex unordered complete flag manifold} \(\overline{\mathrm{Fl}}_{n}(\mathbb{C})\) is defined as \(U(n)/U(1) \wr S_{n} \cong \mathrm{Fl}_{n}(\mathbb{C})/S_{n}\).

In this paper under review, the authors consider the cohomology of these \textit{unordered} complete flag manifolds which have received less attention from algebraic topologists so far. More concretely, based on the previous work [\textit{L. Guerra}, Algebr. Geom. Topol. 23, No. 7, 3221--3292 (2023; Zbl 1530.20124)] concerning the cohomology of \(B_{n}\) and \(B_{n}^{+}\), its ``alternating subgroup'', and elaborate computations of spectral sequences associated with various fibrations involving \(\overline{\mathrm{Fl}}_{n}(\mathbb{R})\) and \(\overline{\mathrm{Fl}}_{n}(\mathbb{C})\), they describe the mod \(2\) cohomology of \(\overline{\mathrm{Fl}}_{n}(\mathbb{R})\) explicitly for \(n = 3, 4, 5\), as well as the mod \(2\) cohomology of \(\overline{\mathrm{Fl}}_{3}(\mathbb{C})\). Furthermore, using their result, they improve the estimate of the number of \textit{Auerbach bases} of a finite dimensional Banach space. Here an Auerbach basis of an \(n\)-dimensional Banach (real or complex) space \(X\) means a biorthogonal system of vectors \(x_{1}, \dots, x_{n} \in X\) and linear functionals \(x_{1}^{*}, \ldots, x_{n}^{*} \in X^{*}\) such that \(||x_{i}|| = ||x_{i}^{*}|| = 1\) for \(i = 1, \ldots, n\). Using topological methods including Lusternik--Shnirelmann theory, \textit{A. Weber} and \textit{M. Wojciechowski} [Commun. Contemp. Math. 19, No. 6, Article ID 1750016, 19 p. (2017; Zbl 1408.46013)] proved that an \(n\)-dimensional Banach space \(X\) has at least \(1 + n(n-1)/2\) different Auerbach bases. The explicit computations in this paper give an improvement of this result for lower dimensions \(n = 3, 4\), and \(5\).
